info.name: MovieDB_store API
info.description:
Endpoint tests for the MovieDB_store microservices, routed through the API gateway on :8760.

## Before running
1. Start Eureka, the gateway and the four services.
2. Set `idToken` to a current Firebase ID token. The gateway validates it and injects a `uid` header downstream, so anything user-scoped (cart, orders, bookmarks, addresses) returns nothing useful without it.

## Order
Run the folders top to bottom. `1. Health & Identity` proves everything is up; `2. Movie Catalog` captures `movieId` and `castId` into collection variables that later requests reuse.

## Note on gateway paths
Requests use `/{service-id}/...`, which the discovery locator serves. The hand-written `/movies/**` style routes in the gateway config have no StripPrefix filter, so they reach the service with the prefix intact and match nothing there.

item.name: 2. Movie Catalog
item.description: Read-only. Captures movieId and castId for later folders.

exec: pm.test("array of at most 6 (default limit)", () => { pm.expect(rows).to.be.an("array").that.is.not.empty; pm.expect(rows.length).to.be.at.most(6); });
pm.test("slim rows: id, movieId, title, year, poster, ratings only", () => rows.forEach(r => pm.expect(Object.keys(r)).to.have.members(["id", "movieId", "title", "year", "poster", "ratings"])));
pm.test("titles starting with the text rank first", () => pm.expect(rows[0].title.toLowerCase().startsWith("bat")).to.be.true);

item.name: Autocomplete with blank text is empty

exec: pm.test("rows carry id, name, roles, knownFor, films", () => rows.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.id).to.match(/^nm\d+$/); pm.expect(r.name).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(r.roles).to.be.an("array").that.is.not.empty; pm.expect(r.knownFor).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(r.films).to.be.above(0); }));
pm.test("a word of the first name starts with the text", () => pm.expect(/(^|[\s\-.])nolan/i.test(rows[0].name)).to.be.true);
// Untitled stub records have prices too; price searches must leave them out.

request.description: The movie's precomputed recommendations, best first; takes the Mongo id or the IMDb id. (It used to answer 500, then any movies sharing the first genre.)

exec: pm.test("20 recommendations, 5 on this page", () => { pm.expect(page.totalElements).to.eql(20); pm.expect(page.content).to.have.lengthOf(5); });
pm.test("best first: The Dark Knight leads to Batman Begins", () => pm.expect(page.content[0].title).to.eql("Batman Begins"));
pm.test("lists every critic and user source", () => { pm.expect(counts.critic).to.have.all.keys("rt", "metacritic"); pm.expect(counts.user).to.have.all.keys("imdb", "letterboxd", "metacritic"); });

pm.test("The Dark Knight has reviews from all five", () => [counts.critic.rt, counts.critic.metacritic, counts.user.imdb, counts.user.letterboxd, counts.user.metacritic].forEach(n => pm.expect(n).to.be.above(0)));

request.description: Reviews collected from other sites, per source (The Dark Knight, by IMDb id). The page uses it to show only the sources with content.

exec: pm.test("rows are Rotten Tomatoes reviews in the shared critic shape", () => page.content.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.source).to.eql("rt"); pm.expect(r.movieId).to.eql("tt0468569"); pm.expect(r.state).to.be.oneOf(["fresh", "rotten"]); pm.expect(r.topCritic).to.be.a("boolean"); pm.expect(r).to.include.keys("critic", "publication", "score", "scoreNormalized", "sentiment", "text", "url", "date"); }));
pm.test("newest first", () => { const d = page.content.map(r => r.date).filter(Boolean); pm.expect(d).to.eql([...d].sort().reverse()); });

item.name: Critic reviews: Metacritic, highest score first

exec: pm.test("rows are Metacritic reviews", () => page.content.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.source).to.eql("metacritic"); pm.expect(r.sentiment).to.be.oneOf(["positive", "mixed", "negative"]); pm.expect(r.state).to.be.null; }));
pm.test("scores descend", () => { const s = page.content.map(r => r.scoreNormalized); pm.expect(s).to.eql([...s].sort((a, b) => b - a)); });

pm.test("rows are IMDb reviews with an author and a rating out of 10", () => page.content.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.source).to.eql("imdb"); pm.expect(r.rating).to.be.within(1, 10); pm.expect(r.user.id).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(r.user.name).to.be.a("string"); pm.expect(r.url).to.include("imdb.com"); }));

item.name: User reviews: Letterboxd, most liked first

exec: pm.test("rows are Letterboxd reviews", () => page.content.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.source).to.eql("letterboxd"); pm.expect(r.liked).to.be.a("boolean"); pm.expect(r.user.name).to.be.a("string"); }));
pm.test("likes descend", () => { const l = page.content.map(r => r.likes); pm.expect(l).to.eql([...l].sort((a, b) => b - a)); });
pm.test("rows are Metacritic user reviews", () => page.content.forEach(r => { pm.expect(r.source).to.eql("metacritic"); pm.expect(r.rating).to.be.within(0, 10); }));

item.description: Things that should fail, and checks on responses that must not regress.

item.name: Unknown movie id returns an error

exec: pm.test("is a client or server error", () => pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.oneOf([400,404,500]));
// Routes are private unless listed as public, so without a token even an
// unknown one answers 401 (which also doesn't reveal which routes exist).
// Sent with no Authorization header (and a forged uid header), so the
// gateway must refuse it rather than pass the uid through.
